descriptionChirho: To see with the eyes, perceive visually; the basic sense of physical sight, whether actively or passively noticing what is before one.
To look at something or someone intentionally, directing one's gaze with focused attention; often translated 'look at' or 'mirando/tazama' rather than simply 'see.'
Imperative use directing hearers to look, observe, or pay attention to something being pointed out, without the connotation of warning against danger.
Imperative use warning hearers to be on guard against something dangerous or deceptive; translated 'beware,' 'watch out,' 'take heed,' Arabic 'احذروا,' Korean '조심하라,' Swahili 'jihadharini.'
Middle/passive sense: to be seen, be visible, be perceived; of things that are apparent or manifest to observers.
To see in the sense of witnessing or experiencing something that will come to pass; used in future-tense declarations about what one will see or behold.
Imperfect tense sense of sustained, intent gazing or staring, often at a departing or ascending figure.
